findings.title: Notification preferences are mutated by an unprotected GET request
findings.body: The new GET unsubscribe route immediately saves notification preferences for the session's current user, without a recipient token or a POST confirmation. Rails CSRF protection does not protect GET requests, so another site can navigate a logged-in user to this URL and silently downgrade or mute notifications for a topic. Keep GET read-only and perform the change through a CSRF-protected request (or an appropriately validated recipient-specific unsubscribe token).

findings.title: Direct save allows automatic tracking to undo unsubscribe
findings.body: The unsubscribe action updates notification_level directly and saves the TopicUser without setting notifications_reason_id. For users whose topic tracking was automatic and whose reason is still nil, TopicUser.update_last_read explicitly restores tracking once the reading-time threshold is exceeded. Consequently, reading the topic after unsubscribing can undo this explicit preference. Use TopicUser.change, as set_notifications does, so the user_changed reason and notification-change metadata are recorded.

findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when the current user has no TopicUser record
findings.body: TopicUser.find_by can return nil for a visible topic the current user has never visited. This can happen when an email link is opened while logged into a different account or when a forwarded link is opened. The action then dereferences tu.notification_level and returns a server error instead of handling the unsubscribe. Resolve the default notification level and create the user's preference record when none exists.

findings.title: Client-side entry never performs the unsubscribe operation
findings.body: The Ember unsubscribe route only loads the ordinary topic view through PostStream.loadTopicView; it never calls the unsubscribe endpoint or changes the notification level. When this URL is entered through client-side navigation, the Rails HTML GET action does not run, yet the template tells the user they will stop receiving notifications. Ensure this flow explicitly performs the preference change rather than relying on an initial full-page server request.
